verses.zh: 耶和华作王！他以威严为衣穿上；耶和华以能力为衣，以能力束腰，世界就坚定，不得动摇。
verses.en: The Lord reigns.He is robed in majesty.The Lord is robed;he wears strength around his waist.[NOTE:1] Indeed, the world is established; it cannot be moved.
notes: Psalm 93. The psalmist affirms that the Lord is the king of the universe who preserves order and suppresses the destructive forces in the world.

verses.zh: 你的宝座从太初立定；你从亘古就有。
verses.en: Your throne has been secure from ancient times;you have always been king.[NOTE:1]
notes: Strength is compared here to a belt that one wears for support. The Lord’s power undergirds his rule.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，大水扬起，大水发声，波浪澎湃。
verses.en: The waves[NOTE:1] roar, O Lord,the waves roar,the waves roar and crash.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “from antiquity [are] you.” As the context suggests, this refers specifically to God’s royal position, not his personal existence.
The Hebrew noun translated “waves” often refers to rivers or streams, but here it appears to refer to the surging waves of the sea (see v. 4, Ps 24:2).

verses.zh: 耶和华在高处大有能力，胜过诸水的响声，洋海的大浪。
verses.en: Above the sound of the surging water,[NOTE:1] and the mighty waves of the sea,the Lord sits enthroned in majesty.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the waves lift up, O Lord, the waves lift up their voice, the waves lift up their crashing.”

Heb “mighty waters.”sn The surging waters here symbolizes the hostile enemies of God who seek to destroy the order he has established in the world (see Pss 18:17; 29:3; 32:6; 77:20; 144:7; Isa 17:13; Jer 51:55; Ezek 26:19; Hab 3:15). But the Lord is depicted as elevated above and sovereign over these raging waters.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，你的法度最的确；你的殿永称为圣，是合宜的。
verses.en: The rules you set down[NOTE:1] are completely reliable.[NOTE:2] Holiness[NOTE:3] aptly adorns your house, O Lord, forever.[NOTE:4]
notes: Traditionally “your testimonies.” The Hebrew noun עֵדוּת (ʿedut) refers here to the demands of God’s covenant law. See Ps 19:7.
The rules you set down. God’s covenant contains a clear, reliable witness to his moral character and demands.
Holiness refers here to God’s royal transcendence (see vv. 1-4), as well as his moral authority and perfection (see v. 5a).
